Can AI make new photos of your face for thumbnails?

Round 1, 2026-11-24. 31 images from two Google image models, each judged beside real stills from the A2P video. Green outline = real. Everything else is generated.

Verdict: ready with a human check.

At thumbnail size the generated faces read as you. On the winning model 7 of 9 images came out usable; the misses, and most of the Pro model's images, show a tell at full size to someone who knows you: a darker beard along the jaw, deeper lines at the eyes, redrawn teeth, or a wrong arm. So: generate two or three, pick one, never publish unseen. The judge here only knows your face from this footage, so your own two-minute look at this page is the real test.

4. What was learned

What worked

  • Put the real still with the closest expression first and call it the main identity reference.
  • Describe the face in plain words: broad round face, short nose, light strawberry-blond stubble, pale skin.
  • Ask for the same camera distance and the same bright, flat light as the references.
  • Say what must not be added: wrinkles, a tan, a darker beard.
  • Describe a pointing direction by the picture edge, never by "his right".
  • Waist-up framing, so the cutout sits at the right height in the thumbnail tool.

What failed

  • "85 mm studio portrait, key light from the left": a sharper, longer-faced cousin.
  • "Visible pores and fine lines": the model aged you.
  • Building a smile from a neutral still: more drift than starting from a smiling still.
  • The Pro model swings: one good smile, then a cousin, from the same prompt.
  • Pointing needed three prompt versions, and the fast model still used the wrong arm.
  • A "studio relight" of a real still added a tan and darkened the beard.

What would raise quality most: a 10 minute photo shoot

  • Phone rear camera in photo mode (not video), plain wall, window light or the softbox, eye level, black t-shirt.
  • Faces: neutral, soft smile, big smile, laugh, surprised, skeptical. Front, then turned a little left and right.
  • Poses: point left, point right, thumbs up, both fists, hand on chin, open palms, holding the phone.
  • Why: today's references are video frames with no pore detail, so the model invents the skin, the beard colour and the teeth. Sharp photos remove that guess, and the real pose shots may be good enough to use directly.
